action_items: MINOR NOTE (not a bug): spec for (a) says clicking a blocked stepper button should show a toast. Current impl uses HTML `disabled={jumpBlocked}` which prevents the click handler firing entirely — so the toast branch in the onClick is unreachable. This is functionally stronger (button also has opacity-40 and section-a-gaps counter next to Next). If a toast is strictly required for a11y screen readers, drop the `disabled` attr and rely on the onClick guard + `aria-disabled='true'`.

SEED DATA: Test intentionally locked PMC-NOT-2026-0020 (both envelopes) to verify (d). Envelope locking is irreversible by design — do not treat as regression. Bid PMC-BID-MANUAL-3C8D under this notice can no longer be scored.
critical_code_review_comments: EvaluationPanel.jsx uses `useRef` to share validation errors from RubricEditor back to the parent (rubricErrorsRef). This works but is a leaky pattern — child mutates parent's ref during render (`if (errorRef) errorRef.current = errors` at RubricEditor line 26). Consider lifting the canSave/errors state to the parent, or using an onValidate(errors) callback in useEffect instead. Render-phase side effects are a React strict-mode footgun.

reports.py post_snapshot wraps the entire snapshot_to_disk() in try/except — but snapshot_to_disk itself already collects per-file errors into `errors[]`. The outer wrapper only catches truly catastrophic failures (mkdir failure, import error). Both layers work, but consider documenting that ok=false with a single '*' error means catastrophic vs per-file failures.

RegistrationResume.jsx line 172: `disabled={jumpBlocked}` on stepper buttons blocks the click event so the toast in the onClick is unreachable. If a toast is intentional, use aria-disabled + onClick guard (see action item).
